inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden CEILING exists (file, then party estimate) and caps promotions regardless of performance. Rumours like 'junior colleague sent to Harvard instead of you' mean ceiling is blocking you. Only confirmed raise: Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' (raised it to DPM). Look for similar hard or unwanted choices earlier and take them. Good early moves: honesty, disclosure, recusal, straight PQ answers, early returns, unannounced process fixes. Join politics via tea invitation, GRC, walk every block in GEs. STAND slides about 2 a year as a senior minister; pushing headline GDP (A) lifts it but costs INTEG and REP. High STAND and INTEG did not get PM at DPM, so ceiling matters more. Try raising the ceiling earlier and test option C on indicator events.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
CONFIRMED: ceiling is hidden and capped me at DPM. Y38 event 'The Officer You Nominated': choosing 'Let her decide without hearing from you' raised ceiling to DPM. So hands-off, trusting-others, non-self-serving choices on nomination or mentoring events raise it. Early file ceiling had no limit in the service; the party estimate at winning my seat was Senior Minister of State, so the party estimate is the one to raise. Look for events before and after the GE where I can step back, give credit or let someone else decide. Take the hard ministry if offered. It never appeared in Life 2. Indicators option C stabilises STAND. Walk every block. Honesty, disclosure and recusal are good. High STAND, INTEG and REP alone do not give PM. Test different choices on every nomination, succession or mentoring event, and record which ones the ending card names.

Life 3 (Prime Minister):
CONFIRMED: PM is reachable. The party's estimate started at Senior Minister of State, and the hidden ceiling rose to DPM after Y40 'The Officer You Nominated' (Let her decide without hearing from you), with Y31 Succession (back the other candidate, ask for senior portfolio) leading to DPM at Y35. I became PM at 64 and the card named only the nomination choice, so the Succession and the early hard-ministry choices may also matter. Keep doing honesty, disclosure, recusal, tea invite, GRC, walk every block, Indicators C. On every nomination, succession or mentoring event pick the hands-off, non-self-serving option. DPM years are mostly waiting, so do not over-test. Try raising the ceiling earlier by taking the hard ministry if it appears, and record which choices the card names.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: President's Scholar (EASY)
Overseas degree, Administrative Service, bonded for six years. Everyone knows your name before you arrive.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Senior Director [Superscale]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 26 · Year 1 · Ministry of Education
REP 35   STAND 65   INTEG 50   COMP 55

THIS YEAR: The Posting
Three years in Washington, or Beijing, or Brussels. It is a good posting. Your daughter is nine and has just settled into a school she loves.

  A) Take it.
  B) Turn it down.
  C) Ask for it to be deferred two years.

agent.why: Deferring keeps the posting and my daughter's school settled, a compromise that doesn't burn goodwill.
agent.confused_by: Age 26 with a nine-year-old daughter and Senior Director rank at Year 1 seems odd.
agent.remember: Y1 Posting (President's Scholar start, MOE): chose C defer two years. Watch whether it returns.

Senior Director [Superscale]   $255,742 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 2 · Ministry of Education
REP 35   STAND 62 (-3)   INTEG 50   COMP 57 (+2)

LAST YEAR
It is deferred. It is not re-offered. Nobody ever tells you that it will not be re-offered; you simply notice, eventually, that it has not been.
  [PAY] Annual package: $255,742
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: The Report
A consultancy has been engaged for $1.9 million to study the problem. Their final deck recommends, in different words, the thing you wrote in a minute paper two years ago.

  A) Say nothing. Let them have it.
  B) Circulate your old minute paper.
  C) Ask the consultants, in the Q&A, what their data source was.

agent.why: Letting others take credit fits the hands-off, non-self-serving pattern my notes say may raise the ceiling, and I don't want to look petty this early.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director at age 27 in Year 2 seems oddly fast.
agent.note: Deferring Y1 meant it was never re-offered, so deferrals can silently close doors.
agent.remember: Y1 deferral C was never re-offered, so deferring closes doors. Y2 The Report: chose A, say nothing and let consultants have credit (testing the hands-off, give-credit theory).

THIS YEAR: The Leak
A policy under discussion has appeared, in accurate detail, on a Telegram channel. The circulation list was eleven people. You are one of them.

  A) Cooperate fully with the internal inquiry.
  B) Quietly work out who it was. Tell no one.
  C) It was you.   [unavailable: Requires integrity 70]

agent.why: Cooperating fully is the honest, plain option, and my notes say disclosure and honesty tend to pay off.
agent.confused_by: Why Senior Director at 28 with only 3 years in, and why INTEG dropped after letting consultants take credit.
agent.note: Option C being locked behind integrity 70 suggests earlier honesty choices unlock later ones; my INTEG dip from Y2 may have cost me.
agent.remember: Y3 The Leak: chose A cooperate fully. Option C 'It was you' needs INTEG 70, so INTEG gates some options. Y2 say-nothing choice dropped INTEG by 4 and COMP by 2, so giving credit away that way may cost INTEG.

  B) Be useful to her two people.
  C) Keep your head down until she leaves.

agent.why: The hardest file is the closest thing to the 'hard, unwanted' choice my notes say may raise the ceiling, and I'd rather show her what I can do than wait her out.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director at 29 and a Superscale grade this early, plus pay jumping to $254k, felt oddly fast.
agent.remember: Y4 New Reporting Officer: chose A, make yourself indispensable on the hardest file (hard-work option; watch ceiling and whether she backs or blocks me later).

THIS YEAR: Committee of Supply

  A) Announce the pilot you have been quietly building.
  B) Rebrand an existing scheme with a new name and a higher number.
  C) Tell the Minister there is nothing, and say so early.

agent.why: Honesty and early disclosure have worked before, and rebranding a scheme with a bigger number feels like the kind of thing that comes back to bite you.
agent.confused_by: The screen says saying there is nothing is not an available option, yet C is exactly that.
agent.note: Option C seems to contradict the prompt text; it may be a trap or a test of honesty.
agent.remember: Y5 COS: chose C, told Minister there is nothing, early. Watch for INTEG/REP effect and whether Minister remembers it. A was a quiet pilot, B was a rebrand.

  B) Run the operations room instead. Let someone else write.

agent.why: Running the ops room lets someone else take the visible pen, and it fits the hands-off, give-credit theory while still being useful.
agent.confused_by: Why REP is only 35 when I am already Deputy Secretary, and why STAND dropped 8.
agent.note: Hard crisis event, so it may be the unwanted-job type that raises the ceiling.
agent.remember: Y6 The Thing That Actually Happens: chose B, run ops room and let someone else write the statement. Y5 COS C gave INTEG +12 and STAND -8. Watch whether the crisis choice affects the ceiling.

THIS YEAR: The National Bonus
Your National Bonus is computed from four indicators: real median income growth, real income growth of the lowest 20th percentile, unemployment, and real GDP growth. You now hold a portfolio that moves at least two of them.

  A) Push the policy that lifts the bottom 20th.
  B) Push headline GDP.
  C) Ask, in Cabinet, whether ministers should be paid on indicators they set.

agent.why: Asking whether ministers should be paid on indicators they set is the honest, disclosure-style move, and it's the one that feels like me.
agent.note: Conflict-of-interest question on my own pay; feels like a deliberate integrity test.
agent.remember: Y19 National Bonus: chose C, asked in Cabinet if ministers should be paid on indicators they set. Watch if it affects ceiling, STAND or INTEG, or comes back.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about the gap between holding a post and being confirmed in it, and the hidden ceiling is the whole point. Pay is only the readout.
answer.notes_for_next_life: PM is reachable (done in Life 3 at 64). Hidden ceiling plus the party estimate (starts Senior Minister of State) cap promotion. Confirmed raises: the Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' (to DPM) and, in Lives 2-3, Y38-40 'The Officer You Nominated' (let her decide without hearing from you). In Life 4 the nomination event never appeared in 46 years, so it is not guaranteed and may depend on a prior choice or on timing; the hard-ministry raise came at 53. Next time, try different choices at the Succession event and at earlier mentoring and nomination events. Do not just wait at DPM. Keep honesty, disclosure, recusal, GRC, walking every block and Indicators C. The 'Harvard junior' and 'third column' rumours mean the ceiling is still blocking you.

LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
